implementation_notes: .NET supplies the endpoint structure: RabbitMQ.Client's EventingBasicConsumer/AsyncEventingBasicConsumer exposes Received/ReceivedAsync events and BasicConsumeAsync(queue, autoAck, consumer) binds them to a channel, so the endpoint class only wraps IConnection/IModel, converts ea.Body into application types and owns ack/nack. Service Bus-style brokers are handled the same way by their processor types (for example ServiceBusProcessor), and MassTransit-style frameworks go one step further by generating the consumer; the classic hand-written structure returns only when the protocol client is used without such a consumer abstraction.
pitfalls: autoAck: true acknowledges on delivery, so a crash inside the handler loses the message; keep manual acknowledgement and ack only after the handler succeeds.
RabbitMQ.Client channels are not thread-safe: do not publish or ack from several threads on one channel, and never let the consumer callback touch another channel's state without serialisation.
An exception escaping the ReceivedAsync handler tears down the connection; catch, nack and let a supervisor rebuild the consumer.
